problem: The wording 'forgetting return before the recursive call' is misleading. It suggests the position of return matters, when the real mistake is writing n × factorial(n−1) as a bare statement with no return at all in the recursive case. A student may place return only in front of the call and still be confused about where it belongs.
fix: Forgetting return in the recursive case, for example writing n * factorial(n-1) as a bare statement, makes the function return None instead of the factorial.

problem: Tail recursion is listed as a topic to search for, but Python does not optimise tail calls. A reader may assume a tail-recursive version of a deep function will avoid the recursion limit, which is false in Python.
fix: Add one sentence: Python does not optimise tail calls, so a tail-recursive function still uses one frame per call and can still hit the recursion limit.

where: Figure (fib(4) tree) aria text and caption
problem: The aria text says the repeated calls give '3', which can be read as three repeated calls rather than the value fib(4) = 3. The caption also only says the calls appear 'in more than one branch' without giving the counts already stated in section 2.
fix: Aria: 'Recursion tree for fib(4): fib(2) is called twice and fib(1) three times; the final value is fib(4) = 3.' Caption: mention fib(2) appears twice and fib(1) three times.

problem: The sentence 'A call to fib(n) makes two recursive calls' is stated without the exception for the base cases n = 0 and n = 1, where no recursive call is made. Read literally it contradicts the base cases given in the same paragraph.
fix: For n ≥ 2 a call to fib(n) makes two recursive calls; fib(0) and fib(1) return at once without calling.
